After weeks of only enforcing a weekly usage cap, OpenAI today announced it will restore the 5-hour usage limit for Codex and ChatGPT Work for Plus subscribers. Details below.

ChatGPT Plus subscribers' 5-hour usage limit restored

OpenAI's head of Codex and ChatGPT engineering Thibault "Tibo" Sottiaux announced tonight that starting tomorrow (the 25th), the 5-hour usage limit for Codex and ChatGPT Work will be restored for Plus subscribers.

When users reach the 5-hour or weekly usage cap, they can either wait for the next cycle to reset their usage, or purchase additional credits. OpenAI will also occasionally reset users' limits for free, and stored reset counts can be obtained through designated promotional campaigns and referral offers.

However, in the past few weeks, OpenAI temporarily removed the 5-hour usage cap for Codex and ChatGPT Work, keeping only the weekly limit.

During this period, the company also reset users' weekly usage multiple times in advance to celebrate milestones, including these two (now merged) platforms reaching an additional one million active users.

However, Tibo explained tonight on X:

"Tomorrow we will restore the 5-hour cap for ChatGPT Work and Codex on Plus accounts. I mentioned this before, but then postponed it. This is necessary because (1) the 5-hour cap allows us to allocate compute resources more smoothly, thereby keeping the weekly usage plans generous; (2) most Plus users are relatively casual new users, but they also unconsciously burn through a whole week's usage, then feel confused, resulting in a not-so-good experience. Over the next few months, we will continue to maintain the 5-hour cap suspension arrangement for Pro $100 and Pro $200 subscriptions."

Tibo made no mention of any changes to enterprise or education accounts, which currently use a separate credit-based usage system.

Will the restoration of the 5-hour cap on ChatGPT Work and Codex affect you? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
